name: Bangladesh
shortSummary: India played a decisive role in Bangladesh's 1971 independence and built a close partnership through the Sheikh Hasina era, but relations have become more complex since the August 2024 political transition in Dhaka.
complexity: Ties were historically close under Sheikh Hasina, who took refuge in India after being ousted in August 2024. The interim government under Muhammad Yunus has taken a more cautious posture toward New Delhi, straining an otherwise deep relationship.

majorAreasOfCooperation.description: Rail, road and inland waterway links to India's northeast transit through Bangladesh.
Cross-border power transmission and Indian-financed energy projects.

majorChallenges.title: Political transition uncertainty
majorChallenges.description: The interim government's posture toward India remains less predictable than under the previous administration.

majorChallenges.title: Teesta water sharing
majorChallenges.description: A long-pending river water-sharing agreement remains unresolved.

recentDevelopments.title: Fall of the Hasina government
recentDevelopments.description: Sheikh Hasina resigned amid mass protests and took refuge in India; an interim government under Muhammad Yunus assumed charge in Dhaka.
recentDevelopments.whyItMatters: Ended a 15-year period of unusually close India-Bangladesh alignment and introduced significant uncertainty into one of India's most important regional relationships.

recentDevelopments.title: Relations remain cautious under the interim government
recentDevelopments.description: Engagement between New Delhi and the interim Dhaka administration continued but with a more guarded tone, including friction over Hasina's status and minority-rights rhetoric.
recentDevelopments.whyItMatters: The relationship has shifted from a strategic anchor to one requiring active, careful management.

historicalEvents.title: Bangladesh Liberation War
historicalEvents.description: India provides military and diplomatic support to the Bangladesh liberation movement, intervening decisively against Pakistan.

historicalEvents.title: Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Peace
historicalEvents.description: India and Bangladesh sign a 25-year friendship treaty shortly after independence.

historicalEvents.title: Ganges Water Treaty
historicalEvents.description: A 30-year treaty on sharing Ganges waters at the Farakka Barrage is signed.

historicalEvents.title: Land Boundary Agreement Implementation
historicalEvents.description: India and Bangladesh exchange enclaves, resolving a decades-old border dispute via the 100th Constitutional Amendment.

historicalEvents.title: Fall of the Hasina Government
historicalEvents.description: Sheikh Hasina resigns amid mass protests and takes refuge in India; an interim government under Muhammad Yunus assumes charge, complicating bilateral ties.
historicalEvents.impact: Bilateral relationship enters a more uncertain phase amid rhetoric over minority rights and Hasina's extradition.

agreements.name: Land Boundary Agreement
agreements.description: Exchange of enclaves along the India-Bangladesh border.

agreements.name: Ganges Water Treaty
agreements.description: Sharing arrangement for Ganges river waters at Farakka.

defenceCooperation.name: Bilateral military exercises (SAMPRITI)
defenceCooperation.description: Annual army-to-army exercise between India and Bangladesh.

multilateralRelations.detail: Joint member working on regional connectivity and trade facilitation.
